children: President Donald Trump said he expects U.S. negotiators to hold further talks with Iran this week, signaling that diplomatic efforts remain active despite Washington’s rejection of Tehran’s latest proposal.

Trump told Axios in a phone interview Sunday that he anticipates additional negotiations. Two regional sources told the news outlet that another round of indirect discussions could take place as soon as Monday.

The expected talks follow negotiations last week involving U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Qatar has been serving as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran.

Trump on Saturday rejected an Iranian proposal that called for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting nuclear negotiations in exchange for the U.S. lifting its naval blockade, easing restrictions on Iranian oil sales and restoring a regional ceasefire.
Iran has continued to push for a diplomatic solution. Araghchi said Sunday that Tehran remains prepared for negotiations despite Trump's rejection of its proposal.

Renewed talks could ease some of the geopolitical risk premium affecting oil, shipping and broader financial markets. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global energy supplies, and disruptions since the conflict began have contributed to higher energy costs and economic uncertainty.

Any sign of progress toward reopening the waterway could put downward pressure on oil prices and benefit industries sensitive to fuel and transportation costs. A breakdown in negotiations or renewed military action could have the opposite effect, increasing the risk of further disruption to energy supplies.

The prospect of more talks doesn’t indicate that an agreement is close. Iran has focused on the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. blockade, while Washington is seeking concessions over Tehran's nuclear program. Regional mediators are continuing efforts to narrow those differences.
Trump said last week that he believed an eventual settlement was possible, while maintaining that Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon.

For markets, the next round of negotiations could provide an important indication of whether the conflict is moving toward de-escalation or another period of heightened military and energy-market risk.

title: Trump expects more US-Iran talks this week as diplomacy continues
